chunks: From him, from Aḥmad, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Maḥmūd, who said:

I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “The Christian slave-girl serves you, while you know that she is Christian; she does not perform wudu (ablution) and does not perform ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah.” He said: “There is no harm; she washes her hands.”

key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ: the slave-girl or female servant being discussed
key_terms.جَنَابَةٍ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or no objection

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Christian servant who does not perform wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) to serve a Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal question posed to al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding a Christian slave-girl serving despite not observing Islamic ritual purification. The Imam عليه السلام replies that there is no problem, indicating practical permissibility when she washes her hands.
